run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T16:52:20Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a low, chronic rate of HTTP 503 responses generated by frontend-proxy for requests to its 'frontend' upstream. In frontend-proxy's Envoy access log every one of these failures is '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' with upstream host 100.70.94.93:8080 (cluster 'frontend'), i.e. the frontend Service, whose only endpoint is pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh (100.96.2.139:8080). The resets are present continuously from the first readable log line at 16:25:34 through 16:56:02, and frontend-proxy ingress ERROR spans are nonzero from ~16:27 to 16:59 (~31 error spans in 35 min, versus ~9.8 ingress spans/s). The alert's annotated value 0.0333 is numerically consistent with two resets inside a one-minute rate window (resets at 16:51:56.864 and 16:51:56.965 precede the 16:52:20 alert by ~24 s), but the alert rule itself is not loaded in Prometheus, so that linkage is an inference. The frontend's own signals show no error spans, no restarts/OOM, steady memory (~120 MB of 200Mi) and steady CPU throttling (25-35% all window), so the deeper reason the frontend side terminates connections before responding is not established: frontend container logs are empty, Jaeger has no traces after ~16:25:15, and Envoy/Node timeout configuration is not readable from any ConfigMap. A fraud-detection OOMKilled restart at 16:17:49 was examined and rejected as a cause: it precedes the errors, is not in the call path of the failing routes, and no checkout error spans exist.

claims.text: At 16:52:20 the frontend-proxy 'ingress' span series had an ERROR-status rate of 0.0111/s against 9.807/s STATUS_CODE_UNSET, while its 'router frontend egress' span series had 0 ERROR rate; the only frontend-proxy error signal is therefore on the ingress (server) spans.

From 16:25:20 to 16:59:42 the frontend-proxy ingress ERROR-span rate fluctuated between 0 and 0.0296/s (5m rate), while ingress UNSET stayed ~9.4-10.4/s; 'router frontend egress' ERROR stayed 0 for every point.

frontend-proxy's Envoy access log shows repeated '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' replies between 16:25:34.988 and 16:39:58.124 (21 occurrences), for GET /api/products/*, /api/cart, /api/recommendations, /api/data/ and / requests; each is an Envoy local 503 with 95 bytes sent and 1-849 ms request duration.

In the 503 lines the Envoy log fields identify the failing upstream: authority 'frontend-proxy:8080', UPSTREAM_HOST '100.70.94.93:8080', UPSTREAM_CLUSTER 'frontend', upstream-local address 100.96.2.218:<ephemeral> (the frontend-proxy pod), downstream-local 100.96.2.218:8080 and downstream-remote 100.96.2.17:<port> (the load-generator pod).

The Service named 'frontend' has ClusterIP 100.70.94.93 on port 8080, and its Endpoints object contains exactly one ready address, 100.96.2.139:8080, which is the podIP of frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh; frontend-proxy's own Service ClusterIP is 100.71.174.230 and its podIP is 100.96.2.218.

Over 16:24:42-16:59:42 the ERROR-status span increase is concentrated on frontend-proxy ingress (31.34); the frontend service's own operations (GET, GET /, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route..., grpc.oteldemo.*) all show 0 error spans, and so do checkout, cart, product-catalog, payment, currency, shipping and accounting.

At 16:52:20 the same per-service view shows frontend-proxy ingress 0.0111/s as the only request-error series other than small flagd EventStream error rates (fraud-detection 0.0037/s, ad 0.0037/s); every frontend span operation is 0.

frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh is Ready with restartCount 0, running since 16:12:29, limits cpu 100m / memory 200Mi; frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p6mgt is Ready with restartCount 0, running since 16:12:29, limits cpu 30m / memory 50Mi; all 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready.

Resource pressure on the two involved pods did not change with the alert: frontend CFS throttling stayed ~0.25-0.35 of periods across 16:29-16:57 and its working set rose only from ~120.5 MiB to ~122.5 MiB; frontend-proxy throttling stayed ~0.045-0.064 and its working set stayed ~19.4 MiB (of a 50Mi limit).

The only readable Jaeger data near the incident is a sampled 20-trace view whose spans are all at 16:25:13-16:25:15; in that slice frontend-proxy 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' spans carry http.status_code 200 and downstream service spans carry rpc.grpc.status_code 0, so no error trace was captured there.

The alert's annotated value 0.0333333 is consistent with the rate of ERROR spans over a one-minute lookback at 16:52:20: the two resets logged at 16:51:56.864 and 16:51:56.965 give 2/60 = 0.0333 per second, matching the value in the alert annotation more closely than the 5m rate (0.0111/s); the alert appears to fire on any nonzero ERROR-span rate rather than on a ratio.

The fault visible in the evidence is that the frontend side (the single endpoint 100.96.2.139:8080 of Service frontend) terminates an already-established HTTP/1.1 upstream connection before sending response headers, which Envoy reports as 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}; a plausible mechanism is a keep-alive/idle-timeout mismatch between Envoy's upstream connection pool and the frontend's HTTP server (or a transient frontend socket/app failure), but the frontend's own reason is not observable from the available logs, spans or configuration.

Because the 503 UC resets are already present at the start of the readable log (16:25:34) and continue at a similar rate to 16:56:02, the condition behind the alert is chronic/low-rate rather than a step change coinciding with 16:52:20; the alert start time is then explained by the threshold/flap behaviour of an 'above 0' error-rate rule evaluated over a short window, not by a new fault introduced at 16:52.

fraud-detection's container restart does not explain this alert: its previous container was OOMKilled (exit code 137) at 16:17:49 and restarted at 16:17:50, i.e. about 9 minutes before the first observable 503 (16:25:34) and 35 minutes before the alert, its only error spans are flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (~2 in 35 min), and checkout — the only caller of fraud-detection — shows 0 error spans while the failing routes (GET /, /api/products/*, /api/data/, /api/cart, /api/recommendations) do not traverse it.

frontend-proxy CPU throttling/ resource exhaustion is not supported as the trigger: its throttled-period fraction was ~0.045-0.064 throughout the window (only ~0.072 even in the 16:50:20-16:52:20 snapshot) and its working set was flat at ~19.4 MiB, with no change at the 16:52:20 alert time, while 503s were already occurring from 16:25.

The downstream effect is narrow: at most ~0.11% of frontend-proxy ingress span rate carried ERROR status at 16:52:20 (0.0111/s vs 9.807/s UNSET) and no frontend, checkout, cart, product-catalog, payment, currency, shipping or accounting operation recorded an error span in the 35-minute window, so nothing observed supports a claim that other services or customers were failing.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in the Prometheus rule set returned by list_prometheus_rules (empty no_data result), so the exact expression, threshold, evaluation interval and 'for' duration cannot be verified; the match between 0.0333 and two errors in one minute is an inference, not a confirmed rule.

Jaeger has no frontend-proxy traces for the incident period: traces_search for 16:55:00-16:59:42 returned no_data, traces_search_by_tags for error=true (16:20-16:26 and 16:30-16:59) and http.status_code="500" (16:25-16:59) returned no_data, and the only sampled traces end at 16:25:15. The span-level detail of the failing requests (frontend server span, error tags, error details) is therefore unknown.

No frontend application logs are available: fetch_pod_logs returned no_data (0 lines read) for frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh in 16:12:00-16:14:30 and in 16:50:00-16:59:42, so there is no application-side error text explaining why the frontend terminates the connections.

Envoy's upstream cluster configuration (idle timeout, keep-alive settings, retry policy) and the frontend's Node.js HTTP server timeouts are not observable: there is no frontend-proxy ConfigMap (only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products exist) and the Deployment specs returned by the API carried no container fields, so the keep-alive/timeout-mismatch hypothesis cannot be confirmed or excluded.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no deployment, configuration or image-change record for the frontend or frontend-proxy workloads could be checked against the incident window.
The Kubernetes events list for otel-demo returned no items at all, so kubelet/network events around 16:51:56 (when three resets occurred within 250 ms) could not be inspected.
next_steps: Inspect the frontend-proxy Envoy cluster definition for the 'frontend' cluster (upstream HTTP/1.1 idle timeout, max_requests_per_connection, retry policy) and compare it with the frontend container's Node.js server keepAliveTimeout/headersTimeout before changing anything.
Enable and capture frontend application/HTTP server logs (or add access logging) so that future upstream connection terminations can be tied to a handler error or an idle-socket close.
Check node i-030aedeb6471c8a81 conntrack table and network statistics for the 16:51:56-16:51:57 burst, and whether kube-proxy DNAT to 100.96.2.139:8080 dropped/reset entries.
Review the RequestErrorRate rule to require a ratio or a threshold above a small floor with a longer 'for' duration, since any single upstream reset currently turns it on.
Consider Envoy retries for idempotent GET requests to the frontend cluster to absorb single-connection resets, after confirming retry safety.
